Got both. Summary of what each harness actually tells its model:

## Claude Code — full worktree *workflow* instructions (tools + prompts)

Claude Code has worktrees as a first-class feature, so the binary carries a lot of instruction text:

**Tool-level (EnterWorktree / ExitWorktree / Agent isolation):**
- `isolation: "worktree"` on Agent — *"gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged)"*; *"otherwise the path and branch are returned in the result"*. Mutually exclusive with `cwd`.
- EnterWorktree: creates fresh worktree; pass `path` instead of `name` to switch into an existing one — *"must appear in `git worktree list` … target must be a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` of the same repository"*. ExitWorktree won't remove worktrees it didn't create; *"keep' leaves the worktree and branch on disk; 'remove' deletes both"*. Outside a git repo it delegates to `WorktreeCreate`/`WorktreeRemove` hooks for VCS-agnostic isolation.
- Workflow tool docs: worktree isolation flagged *"EXPENSIVE (~200–500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel"*.

**Injected system prompt for isolated subagents:**
> "You are running in an isolated git worktree at `<path>` (a separate working copy of the repo). Changes you make here do NOT affect the main working directory or other agents. Work normally — the worktree will be cleaned up automatically if you made no changes, or preserved for review if you did."

**Background-session guard (bgIsolation, default `worktree`):**
- Blocks Edit/Write in the shared checkout until EnterWorktree is called: *"writes to the shared checkout are blocked. Re-spawn this agent with `isolation: "worktree"`, or have the parent call EnterWorktree first so edits land in a worktree instead of the shared checkout"*. Opt-out: `"worktree": {"bgIsolation": "none"}` in `.claude/settings.json`.

**Settings/behavior knobs:**
- `branchFrom`: *"'fresh' (default) branches from origin/<default-branch> for a clean tree. 'head' branches from your current local HEAD"* — applies to `--worktree`, EnterWorktree, and agent isolation.
- `.worktreeinclude` file: untracked files matching it get copied into new worktrees (symlinks skipped).
- Swarm/parallel planning prompt: work units must *"be independently implementable in an isolated git worktree (no shared state with sibling units)"*, and *"All agents must use `isolation: "worktree"` and `run_in_background: true`"*.

## Codex — only defensive *etiquette*, no creation instructions

Codex's system prompt never tells the model to create worktrees — the `~/.codex/worktrees/<hash>/` dirs are made mechanically by the harness (cloud/review tasks), invisible to the prompt. All it has is the "dirty worktree" block in every base prompt variant:

> "You may be in a dirty git worktree.
> - NEVER revert existing changes you did not make unless explicitly requested, since these changes were made by the user.
> - If asked to make a commit … and there are unrelated changes … don't revert those changes.
> - If the changes are in files you've touched recently, read carefully and work with the changes rather than reverting them.
> - If the changes are in unrelated files, just ignore them."

Plus adjacent git rules: never `git reset --hard` / `git checkout --` unprompted, no amend, prefer non-interactive git. And a resume instruction: *"Use the current worktree and external state as authoritative"* — i.e. trust disk over stale conversation context.

**Net difference:** Claude Code instructs the model to *manage* worktrees (create/enter/exit/clean, isolation policy); Codex only instructs the model to *not break* whatever worktree it wakes up in.
